skill.name: prototype
skill.description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
skill.summary: Build disposable logic or UI prototypes that answer a focused design question before production implementation.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.user_title: Build Focused Logic and UI Prototypes
content.value_statement: Design decisions are difficult to evaluate before users can interact with them. This skill builds disposable prototypes that expose state behavior or compare interface variants.
actual_capabilities: Selects a logic or UI workflow based on the design question and surrounding project context.
Builds small terminal interfaces for exercising state models and viewing each transition.
Separates prototype logic from terminal input and rendering through a portable module interface.
Creates three structurally distinct interface variants with URL-based switching on one route.
Documents the tested question, run command, result, and cleanup path.
limitations: Produces disposable code with minimal testing and error handling, so results need production hardening.
Uses in-memory or stubbed data by default and does not validate production persistence.
Depends on the host project's runtime, router, task runner, and component conventions.
Answers one focused question and does not replace full usability or security testing.

use_cases.title: Validate State Transitions
use_cases.description: Exercise difficult business rules through a small terminal interface before committing to an architecture.

use_cases.title: Compare Interface Directions
use_cases.description: Review three structurally different page layouts with the same data and surrounding application context.

use_cases.title: Resolve Team Decisions
use_cases.description: Create an interactive artifact that helps a team select a direction and record why it won.

prompt_templates.title: Test a State Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a logic prototype for [feature]. Use [runtime], show the full state after each action, and provide one run command.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: validate a small set of state transitions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Page Layouts
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three structurally different variants for [page] on its existing route. Reuse current data and add URL-based switching.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare interface structures inside an existing application.

prompt_templates.title: Probe Edge Cases
prompt_templates.prompt: Prototype [workflow] as a pure state module with a thin terminal interface. Include actions for [cases] and expose invalid transitions clearly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: test complex business rules while keeping logic portable.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate an Embedded Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build five distinct variants for [flow] inside [host page]. Keep data loading unchanged, stub mutations, add keyboard switching, and define evaluation criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare a new flow within realistic application context.

output_examples.input: I need to check whether an invitation can be accepted after it expires.
output_examples.output: A terminal prototype displays invitation state and offers expire, accept, revoke, and reset actions. Each action redraws the complete state.

output_examples.input: Show alternatives for the existing billing settings page.
output_examples.output: Three variants appear on the billing route: a summary-first layout, a task-focused layout, and a comparison layout. A bottom switcher changes variants.

best_practices: Write the design question before implementation and keep every prototype focused on that question.
Use existing project tools, routes, data loading, and visual conventions.
Record the winning decision, remove temporary controls, and harden retained code before production.
anti_patterns: Do not treat prototype code as production-ready implementation.
Do not connect interface variants to irreversible production mutations.
Do not create cosmetic variants that preserve the same layout and hierarchy.

faq.question: What types of questions can this skill test?
faq.answer: It tests focused questions about state behavior, business logic, data shape, page structure, and interface hierarchy.

faq.question: Does it produce production-ready code?
faq.answer: No. Prototype code has limited testing and error handling, so retained parts require review and production hardening.

faq.question: How many interface variants does it create?
faq.answer: It creates three variants by default and limits the comparison to five.

faq.question: Can prototype logic be reused?
faq.answer: Yes. A pure logic module can be retained after review, while the terminal interface should be removed.

faq.question: Does it require a specific framework?
faq.answer: No. It follows the host project's existing runtime, router, task runner, and component system.

faq.question: What happens after a direction is selected?
faq.answer: Record the decision, remove losing variants and temporary controls, then rewrite or harden any retained implementation.
